name: Nature vs Urban Sounds: Aesthetic Preference and Sound Recognition
description: Faithful replication of Experiment 2A with the authors' own sounds: each participant is randomly assigned to one of three groups and hears 80 soundscapes (40 nature, 40 urban) in random order, rating how much they like each on a 7-point scale (1 = strongly dislike, 4 = neither dislike nor like, 7 = strongly like). Unaltered group: the original 5-s clips; Scrambled group: the same clips time-domain scrambled (25 ms windows shuffled within 250 ms), which keeps the spectrum but makes sources hard to recognise; Thin-sliced group: the first 100 ms of each clip. Before rating, participants set their volume with 10 s of pink noise, then give age and gender at the end, as in the paper. Rebuilt from Van Hedger, Nusbaum, Heald, Huang, Kotabe & Berman (2019), Cognitive Science 43(5): e12734, with the sound files from the authors' OSF project 4wb27 and the method and wording from the CC0 preprint (doi:10.31234/osf.io/nsqvy). The sound files are used as the authors shared them on OSF; the template is taken down if the authors object. Analysis as in the paper: 2 x 3 mixed ANOVA on mean liking with sound category (nature vs urban, within) and group (unaltered, scrambled, thin-sliced, between); the nature preference should be large for unaltered sounds, smaller for scrambled and absent for thin slices. Differences from the original study: (1) online with any participants rather than US MTurk workers with at least 90 % approval; (2) the sounds are converted from WAV to MP3 (96 kbps) for web playback; (3) the calibration pink noise is generated by us at the same RMS level as the soundscapes, because the original noise file is not on OSF; (4) each sound plays once and the rating unlocks when it ends (the paper does not say whether ratings could be given during playback); (5) the gender options are our wording; (6) the follow-up conditions (Experiment 1 sound identification, Experiment 2B nature/urban classification, Experiment 3 generated noises) are not included. Sound ids: N = nature, U = urban; the letter after it is the authors' file-name code.
author: Van Hedger, Nusbaum, Heald, Huang, Kotabe & Berman
